baslik: A Loose Wire Turned a Signal Green

sahneler.metin: One old wire kept a railway signal showing green.
A packed train crashed into another near Clapham Junction, and thirty five people died.
The signal should have turned red behind the stopped train.
Days earlier, technicians had rewired that signal.
An old wire had not been disconnected or cut back.
It fed false current to the signal.
Afterwards, testers had to be trained and certified.
Signal technicians had to retrain every five years.

aciklama:
Clapham Junction saw a train run into another that had stopped at a signal. The cause: a wiring fault after re-signalling work keeping a signal at green behind a stopped train.

kanitlar.alinti: A total of 35 people died in the collision, while 484 were injured in what is Britain's seventh worst rail disaster in terms of death toll.

kanitlar.iddia: A wiring fault meant the signal showed green when it should have shown red.
kanitlar.alinti: An initial internal investigation showed that a wiring fault meant that the signal would not show a red danger aspect when the track circuit immediately in front of the signal was occupied.

kanitlar.iddia: An old wire had not been disconnected after new signalling work.
kanitlar.alinti: The signalling technician who had done the work had not cut back, insulated or tied back the loose wire, and his work had not been supervised or inspected by an independent person as was required.

kanitlar.iddia: Signal technicians needed to attend refresher courses every five years, and testers needed to be trained and certified.
